sections.label: Mark Cooke, BEng (Hons)
sections.quote: Understanding what happened to the aircraft—<t>and what the records can support.</t>
body: For forty-five years Mark Cooke has worked across military and commercial aviation—as an airframe technician, a CAA and FAA licensed engineer, an overhaul manager and a founder—helping owners, lessors and counsel understand aircraft condition, maintenance history and the contractual obligations attached to them.

items.d: Across military and commercial aircraft environments—from Royal Air Force airframe technician to founder and operator.
EASA Part-66 Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Licence No. 101488 · FAA Airframe & Powerplant Licence No. 257104.
Aircraft Engineering, Kingston University London. Cardiff University Bond Solon Expert Witness Civil Certificate, 2024.
Instructed by both sides, and available as single joint expert. Written reports for aviation matters worldwide.

sections.label: A point of view built over four decades
sections.quote: In aviation, the asset is <t>never just the aircraft.</t>
body: Its condition, maintenance history, technical records, contractual obligations, commercial position and transition requirements have to be understood together. A discrepancy in a maintenance record is rarely only a technical question—it moves value, triggers obligations and decides disputes.
Mark’s work sits at that intersection: establishing what the aircraft and its records actually show, then explaining what that means for the contract and for the asset.
That perspective comes from having done the work. He has held the licence, signed the release to service, run the hangar and built the organisation.

sections.label: The arc of the work
sections.title: Forty-five years spent on the aircraft, <t>then on the business around it.</t>

days.title: Airframe technician
days.body: Ten years across several Royal Air Force bases in the United Kingdom, on the maintenance and rectification of both fixed and rotary wing aircraft. The decade that set the standard for everything after it.

days.title: Licensed engineer to overhaul manager
days.body: Twelve years at one of the largest maintenance facilities in Europe at the time, capable of four widebody aircraft. Inspector Supervisor and UK CAA and FAA licensed engineer, then project manager, then aircraft overhaul manager—responsible for day-to-day operations and roughly two hundred staff.

days.title: Founder and technical director
days.body: Built a consultancy serving major commercial aircraft leasing and asset-management companies, with a team of twenty consultants working transitions, pre-redelivery, pre-purchase and mid-lease audits at locations worldwide.

days.title: Founder, partner and EVP
days.body: Co-founded and built an airworthiness and engine maintenance group from scratch—a CAMO office at Manchester International Airport and an engine maintenance facility at Hawarden Airport, approved by several airworthiness authorities. The group was sold to Sabena Engineering Brussels in 2023.

days.title: Advisor and expert witness
days.body: Advisory services to the commercial aviation industry through 29 Aero Limited, together with expert witness and expert advice services following Cardiff University Bond Solon certification in 2024.

sections.label: For counsel
sections.title: Aviation disputes turn on what the records <t>can actually support.</t>
sections.intro: Aircraft condition, maintenance history and contractual obligation rarely align neatly by the time a matter reaches counsel. Establishing what happened requires someone who has read these records as the person accountable for them—and who can explain the findings plainly to lawyers, arbitrators and tribunals. Mark provides independent analysis, written reports and expert advice in commercial aviation matters. He is instructed by claimants and defendants alike, and is available as a single joint expert.

rows.d: Return conditions, pre-redelivery and redelivery findings, maintenance reserves, transition scope and the technical basis of claims between lessors, operators and purchasers.
Continuing airworthiness compliance, technical record integrity, back-to-birth traceability, maintenance programme adherence, workmanship and maintenance error.
Lease agreements, maintenance agreements and work scopes, MRO and OEM obligations, repossession and recovery, and the commercial consequences of technical findings.

std.label: Standards of practice
items: Instructed under CPR Part 35 — the expert’s duty is to the court, above the instructing party.
Expert evidence in arbitration, including proceedings under the IBA Rules.
Accepts instruction in England & Wales and internationally; written reports worldwide.
Initial response within one business day.
He does not opine on flight operations, piloting or air-traffic control.
